brief: Soft, performance-y everyday clothing for guys and gals who want to go from gym to coffee. Joggers around $90, shorts $65. Want to reach people who've already shown they spend on activewear.

profile.business_summary: DTC brand selling premium, soft, performance-y everyday clothing (such as joggers and shorts) designed to transition from the gym to casual settings, targeting activewear spenders.

relevant_tags.why: Everyday clothing designed for casual transitions like going to coffee.
Yoga practitioners are a core demographic for performance-y everyday clothing.
Shoppers attending fitness classes are highly likely to buy activewear.

persona_conflicts.conflict: Disinterested in luxury-only messaging or vague premium positioning; high price sensitivity.

note_signals.why: Fitness-engaged shoppers are the ideal target audience for activewear.
Users actively spending on self-care and fitness align perfectly with premium activewear buyers.
Conservative brand sensibility may clash with casual, gym-to-coffee activewear.
Comfort-seeking urban professionals are a strong demographic match for everyday performance wear.

config.advertiser_summary: DTC brand selling premium, soft, performance-y everyday clothing (such as joggers and shorts) designed to transition from the gym to casual settings, targeting activewear spenders.

assumptions: No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 60% gross margin (typical for apparel). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($90 x 60% margin x 1.3 orders = $70.20).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $49.14 x click-to-purchase rate (1.0%-3.5% for apparel). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.70 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.38 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts

score 0.69 -> relative fit x1.39 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.37 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts
score 0.30 -> relative fit x0.94 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.93 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $1,300, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $49.14 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
